 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Auburn football returns to Jordan-Hare Stadium today to face the Arkansas Razorbacks in a key SEC showdown.
 The Tigers recently finished the toughest stretch of the season, going 1-3 against four ranked conference foes. Saturday, Auburn begins arguably the most important stretch of its schedule. Auburn, 4-4, needs just two wins to qualify for a bowl game, and a win over Arkansas would make its route to bowl eligibility much easier.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Arkansas (3-5) is looking for its second SEC win of the season after taking down Vanderbilt in Week 7. Arkansas has thrown the ball well in its last two games, which could be a problem for Auburn's defense, which ranks No. 15 in the SEC in pass defense.
 Auburn leads the all-time series over Arkansas, 21-13-1, but the away team has won the last four games in this SEC rivalry played annually since the Razorbacks joined the conference in 1992. Auburn head coach Alex Golesh will also look to grab his first win over Arkansas head coach Ryan Silverfield. Silverfield's Memphis Tigers defeated Golesh's USF Bulls three times during Golesh's tenure in Tampa.
 Follow along for highlights, injury news, key plays, and instant breakdown as Auburn takes on Arkansas in a pivotal SEC showdown.

 Sylvester Smith-Reed, Bryce Deas ruled out for Auburn
 11:30 AM ET, November 7 2026, Taylor Jones 
 Bad news was published Friday in the SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report. Auburn has listed linebacker Bryce Deas and safety Sylvester Smith-Reed out for Saturday's game against the Arkansas Razorbacks. Deas took over production at linebacker for Xavier Atkins, who was dismissed from the team ahead of the Tigers' Week 8 game against LSU. Smith-Reed has 18 tackles, a fumble recovery, and an interception this season.
